title: Choose the VS arena
question: Which structure should carry team setup, the live head-to-head search, and the final result?

options.label: Airlock Arena
options.lineage: opposing ready rooms opening into one match floor
options.thesis: Team setup becomes the arena: two facing rosters lock in, then open around the shared semantic field.
options.viewport: Red and blue team bays own the left and right thirds; a narrow launch seam becomes the live semantic map and match status after ready-up.
options.risk: The theatrical symmetry must collapse into a practical single-column mobile flow.

options.label: Orbital Tug
options.lineage: a central navigation plot pulled by two telemetry rails
options.thesis: The semantic map is the contest itself, with each team’s progress exerting visible pressure from opposite sides.
options.viewport: An oversized semantic field occupies the center; narrow team rails flank it with progress, players, typing, and finish state while your guess console anchors below.
options.risk: A dominant map can crowd the flight log on short laptop screens.

options.label: Timing Lanes
options.lineage: a race-control timing screen with two synchronized lanes
options.thesis: The match reads in one glance as parallel runs toward the same target, without pretending the opponent’s words are visible.
options.viewport: Two full-width team lanes lead with best, average, guesses, hints, and player activity; your flight log and the shared redacted map sit below in a stable work grid.
options.risk: The clarity is exceptional, but it needs a decisive spatial moment to avoid feeling like a dashboard.
